story_text.value:
It's not on their website or Trust center yet, but we received the following breach notification from WorkOS:

We are writing to notify you of a data security incident that we detected on October 30, 2026 and are continuing to investigate. We value your trust and want to keep you informed while our investigation continues.

What Happened

On October 30, 2026, at 16:39 UTC, WorkOS detected anomalous traffic to an internal business system. Our investigation identified evidence the attack was likely driven by ARTEX, an AI-assisted, autonomous penetration testing framework, from IP addresses based in Hong Kong and China.

The unauthorized actor gained access to an internal API used by our sales and marketing tools. Through this service, it was able to access data from our Salesforce and Snowflake instances. These systems hold business contact information, account and commercial information, aggregated and de-identified product usage metrics, marketing contacts, and support tickets. This includes CRM information such as names, email addresses, phone numbers, company mailing addresses, and other business information for WorkOS customers.

We have no evidence that your application data was accessed. We also have no evidence that any production WorkOS services were accessed or impacted. Our current analysis indicates this incident was localized to only CRM and customer support data.

...

story_text.value:
Hey HN,

Like so many other SWEs right now, I am trying to find ways to enhance my development experience without taking away from the quality of my work or the things I find enjoyable about software engineering, especially as one who very much enjoys the act of pulling something together using well crafted code.

I have found (what I think at least) is a maximum of productivity and enjoyment by primarily using Opencode as a pair programmer and wrangling out the general structure of the solution, before doing probably a 35% AI and 65% me pass of actually writing up the code. Has anyone else found success with this technique of development? I have always been someone who very much enjoys writing well written and designed code, and I am evaluating whether I want to stay in the field as I am concerned that there will not be a place for my style of development in the future. I would appreciate it if others could share their techniques for using AI in the workplace to help me evaluate if my current methods are sustainable career-wise, if there are other ways of using AI that I may also enjoy, or if it might be time for me to look into other fields for the remainder of my career.

I don't post here often so I apologize if I have violated some HN posting conventions with my post, just looking for the opinions of other developers in a place with a bit more of a pro-AI slant than the places I usually hang around.

title.value: Ask HN: Techniques for productive AI use in the workspace
